                                      PROJECT NO. 58481

 RULEMAKING TO IMPLEMENT                          § PUBLIC UTILITY COMMISSION
 LARGE LOAD INTERCONNECTION                       §
 STANDARDS UNDER PURA §37.0561                    §            OF TEXAS


                             COMMENTS OF SERENA ENERGY

       Serena Energy (Serena) appreciates the opportunity to submit these comments as a follow

up to two issues discussed at the January 9, 2026, Workshop (Workshop) in this proceeding. First,

Serena recommends the Commission support and ERCOT recognize the use of three-party

agreements when the entity that is certificated or otherwise has the legal authority to provide retail

delivery service to a large load customer is not the same as the entity that will provide transmission

service to interconnect the large load customer. As discussed during the Workshop, these

agreements between the transmission entity, retail entity, and large load customer can provide

clarity as to roles and responsibilities of each party during the interconnection process. Second,

Serena urges the Commission to ensure that provisions of 16 TAC §25.194 adopted in this

proceeding will work in conjunction with ERCOT’s proposed Large Load Batch Study process

and support transparency on the development and implementation of that process.

       Serena Energy is a global energy generator with nearly three gigawatts of installed capacity

across the Americas and has been operating in Texas since 2023 through the Goodnight Wind

Project.

                                          DISCUSSION

       1. The Commission Should Support Development of Three Party Agreements.

       During the discussion in response to Commission Staff Questions 3 and 4 during the

Workshop, and in a couple of instances thereafter, there was a recommendation about the potential

use of three-party agreements between the transmission entity, retail entity, and large load customer
 to provide clarity as to roles and responsibilities of each party during the interconnection process.

For example, such an agreement could be used to clarify the process for posting, maintaining, and

refunding financial security. As the discussion draft rules in this proceeding have suggested, there

may be multiple instances in which the large load customer could be required to pay study fees or

post security. While the normal course of operation would require a customer to pay these fees or

post security with their retail provider, the fees and security in the large load interconnection

process often relate to studies or work performed by the transmission provider and/or ERCOT. It

would be beneficial for all three parties to document in a single agreement roles and responsibilities

regarding these fees and security to ensure that all fees and security are appropriately tracked and

accounted for.

       Serena does not recommend that the Commission adopt model or mandatory forms for

such agreements at this time. Rather, Serena anticipates that affected entities can and will develop

these agreements on their own to meet their needs. However, given the fact that these will be new

to the interconnection process, Commission acknowledgement as to the appropriateness of these

forms will ensure that ERCOT accepts them as well for the purposes for which they are executed,

just as it would a traditional two-party agreement. Specifically, Serena recommends that

presentation to ERCOT of a signed agreement that confirms required security has been posted be

fully recognized by the Commission and ERCOT as substantial evidence of the load to ensure that

studies and analysis will commence in a timely fashion.

       2. The Commission Should Ensure Consistency of the Proposed Rules With
          ERCOT’s Large Load Batch Study Process and Transparency of that Process.

       As the Commission and ERCOT work quickly to adopt regulations and processes to

address the significant number of large load interconnection requests in the ERCOT Region, there

is a potential for inconsistent requirements to develop. This concern was noted several times


                                                                            Serena Comments - Page 2
 during the Workshop. Serena appreciates that the Commission and ERCOT will strive to avoid

any inconsistencies and will endeavor to ensure that the regulations developed in this proceeding

will support the new batch study process ERCOT is developing. However, both efforts are

occurring simultaneously rather than sequentially, so issues may arise. Since one of the goals of

both efforts is to provide greater consistency in the large load interconnection process in ERCOT

regardless of the transmission provider at issue, any inconsistencies between the two processes

also can undermine the realization of that goal.

       Serena also respectfully notes that transparency is critical in the development both of the

regulations in this proceeding and ERCOT’s development of the Large Load Batch Study process.

Serena commends the efforts Commission Staff has made to ensure transparency in this proceeding

by issuing initial questions for comment and then providing two discussion drafts of the proposed

rules and holding the Workshop. Serena also appreciates the comments Commissioners and

ERCOT Staff made during the January 15, 2026, Open Meeting supporting transparency as

ERCOT launches the development of its new process. For large load customers that have been

working many months to be interconnected, the sudden shift to this new batch process may inject

additional uncertainty as to how long it will take to make it through the interconnection process.

Additional uncertainty in what already has been a long and complex process may undermine, rather

than support, the development of large loads in the ERCOT region. Ensuring transparency in the

development of the new batch study process will help reduce uncertainty.

                                         CONCLUSION

       Serena appreciates the opportunity to file these comments and appreciates the efforts of the

Commission Staff, ERCOT, and interested stakeholders to develop new regulations and processes




                                                                         Serena Comments - Page 3
 that will support the development and interconnection of large load customers in the ERCOT

region.
